messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — Elevated 5xx rate detected for service `gateway-proxy` (5xx spike > 12% over baseline). Paging on-call.
pagerduty: Paging Alex (on-call) — Priority P1 (escalation rule 1). Incident channel created.
Alex: got it, acking. jumping in. I'm seeing a sharp spike starting ~3301234400. Graphs: gateway 5xx -> 18%, upstream 502/503. Appears correlated with a config rollout to `edge-route-v2` 2m ago.
Maria: looking at envoy traces — a lot of `retry` attempts followed by upstream 503s. Possible retry amplification: frontend retries + upstream also retries => overload.
Sam: can someone paste the route config? I want to check retry_policy + circuit_breakers.
Ingrid: grabbing config from k8s now.
Ingrid: ```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  route.yaml: |
    - name: edge-route-v2
      match: /api/v1/generate
      retry_policy:
        retry_on: 5xx,connect,refused-stream
        num_retries: 3
        per_try_timeout: 1s
      route:
        cluster: model-serving
        timeout: 30s
```
Reena: that num_retries=3 on a route hitting a backend that already has its own retries looks dangerous under load. If backend latency increases, retries pile up and circuit-breakers never see a stable signal.
Alex: agree. Observed `upstream_response_time` tail increasing, and `pending_requests` on pods goes up. Circuit breaker config on cluster is default (max_connections high, max_pending_requests 1024). We should reduce retries first (fast rollback) and tighten pending request limits.
Sam: immediate mitigation plan:
- disable retries for `edge-route-v2` (set num_retries: 0)
- decrease `max_pending_requests` for `model-serving` cluster to 200
- scale up model-serving by +3 pods if necessary
- if not improved, shift 30% traffic to `edge-route-v1` rollback variant
Who can apply the quick patch?
Ingrid: I can push a patch to the configmap and rollout. Patching now.
Ingrid: ```bash
kubectl patch configmap envoy-route -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"route.yaml":"- name: edge-route-v2\n  match: /api/v1/generate\n  retry_policy:\n    retry_on: none\n    num_retries: 0\n    per_try_timeout: 0s\n  route:\n    cluster: model-serving\n    timeout: 30s\n"}}'
```
Alex: making the change to cluster CB via envoy admin: `curl -X POST http://envoy-admin/model-serving/cluster_config -d '{"max_pending_requests":200}'`
ops-runbook-bot: NOTE — making runtime changes to CB can drop in-flight connections. Proceeding with caution.
Maria: after disabling retries, I'm already seeing a drop in total request volume to upstream and instantaneous 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 9% (10s). Keep watching.
Reena: also turning on route shadow to v1 for 20% in case we need quick traffic shift: `traffic-shift edge-route-v2 -> v1 20%` (done)
Alex: scaling model-serving +2 now: `kubectl scale deployment model-serving --replicas=8 -n inference`
Ingrid: logs from a model pod showing retry storm:
```
[2026-03-15T15:18:22Z] WARN request_id=abcd retrying request after upstream 502
[2026-03-15T15:18:22Z] ERROR request_id=efgh upstream returned 503 TooManyRequests
```
Sam: that's consistent. With retries disabled, we should see fewer inflight, letting circuit breakers tripped earlier and protecting pods.
Maria: metrics at +120s: gateway 5xx now 4.8%, upstream 5xx 3.5%. Latency stable. Good.
Alex: customer impact — degraded for ~3m for ~40% of requests to this route (est). Pages from support: 4 customers reported errors. Sending incident severity update to SRE/eng managers.
Reena: starting a quick RCA note: suspected cause: recent route rollout increased retries for a route whose backend cannot tolerate amplification; combined with permissive circuit-breaker pending queue -> request pileup -> upstream 503 -> more retries -> overload.
Alex: Next steps / action items before handoff:
- Create a small test to validate retry behavior under latency spike (Maria)
- Tighten default cluster circuit-breakers to [max_pending_requests:200, max_connections: 1000] (Sam)
- Add a guard in rollout pipeline that flags non-zero retries when backend has retry semantics (Reena)
- Postmortem doc (Alex)
I'll hand off to Reena for the on-call rotation in 30m.
Reena: taking over monitoring. I have the runbook and will coordinate with infra for a follow-up change. Please add any additional notes here.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook reference: https://intra.redwood/rb/envoy-retry-amplification
Alex: thanks all, resolving immediate mitigation. Will file postmortem template and link to this thread.
Reena: final check at 3301234870: error rates stable at ~2.1% gateway, upstream at 1.8%. Reopening if it resurfaces. Closing active pager.
pagerduty: Incident resolved and acknowledged. No further pages.
